drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What does 'trouble peeing' mean for you: hesitancy, weak stream, burning, frequency, urgency, incontinence, or unable to pass urine?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the symptom pattern guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: Are you unable to pass urine at all, or only passing a small amount with a full painful bladder?
questions.rationale: Inability to void can signal acute urinary retention and needs urgent attention.

questions.text: Is the urine stream weak, slow, or interrupted?
questions.rationale: A weak or interrupted stream points toward obstructive or voiding symptoms.

questions.text: Do you have trouble starting to pee, or do you have to wait before the urine starts?
questions.rationale: Hesitancy helps separate obstructive voiding symptoms from other urinary complaints.

questions.text: Do you have to strain or push to get urine out?
questions.rationale: Straining can suggest outlet obstruction or retention.

questions.text: Are you peeing more often than usual during the day?
questions.rationale: Frequency can reflect infection, irritation, high urine volume, or bladder symptoms.

questions.text: Do you get a sudden strong urge to pee that is hard to hold?
questions.rationale: Urgency helps identify bladder irritation or overactivity.

questions.text: Are you waking up at night to pee? If so, how many times?
questions.rationale: Nocturia can suggest urinary, metabolic, fluid, or medication contributors.

questions.text: Have you been leaking urine or having accidents?
questions.rationale: Incontinence changes the differential and can point to urgency, overflow, or neurogenic causes.

questions.text: Does it burn or hurt when you pee?
questions.rationale: Dysuria can indicate infection, irritation, or inflammation.

questions.text: When did this start, and has it been getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Onset and duration help distinguish acute from chronic urinary symptoms.

questions.text: What color is your urine? Any pink, red, or brown?
questions.rationale: Visible blood can point to infection, stones, trauma, or malignancy.

questions.text: Have you had fever, chills, or sweats with the urinary symptoms?
questions.rationale: Systemic symptoms raise concern for infection or a more serious process.

questions.text: Do you have flank pain, pain in your side or back, or pain that comes in waves?
questions.rationale: Flank pain can suggest kidney involvement or a stone.

questions.text: Do you have lower belly or suprapubic pain or pressure?
questions.rationale: Suprapubic discomfort can occur with bladder irritation or retention.

questions.text: Any penile or vaginal discharge, itching, or sores?
questions.rationale: Discharge or sores can suggest a sexually transmitted infection or local irritation.

questions.text: Have you had any new sexual partners or unprotected sex recently?
questions.rationale: Sexual history helps assess risk for urethritis and related infections.

questions.text: Have you had a catheter, procedure, or other recent instrumentation?
questions.rationale: Recent instrumentation can trigger infection, irritation, or trauma.

questions.text: Have you started any new medicines such as anticholinergics, decongestants, opioids, or diuretics?
questions.rationale: Several medications can cause retention, frequency, or urinary changes.

questions.text: How much are you drinking, and are you using a lot of caffeine or alcohol?
questions.rationale: Fluid and caffeine intake can drive frequency and nocturia.

questions.text: Have you been constipated or having trouble with bowel movements?
questions.rationale: Constipation can worsen urinary symptoms or contribute to retention.

questions.text: Have you ever been told you have an enlarged prostate, BPH, or trouble emptying your bladder before?
questions.rationale: Past voiding problems or BPH can explain current obstructive symptoms.

questions.text: Have you had kidney stones or bladder stones before?
questions.rationale: Prior stones raise the chance that current pain or blood is stone-related.

questions.text: Have you had urinary tract infections before?
questions.rationale: A prior UTI history changes the likelihood of recurrence.

questions.text: Do you have diabetes or high blood sugar?
questions.rationale: Diabetes can increase urinary frequency and infection risk.

questions.text: Is pregnancy possible right now?
questions.rationale: Pregnancy changes the workup and urgency of urinary symptoms.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern can guide reassurance and follow-up questions.

questions.text: Do you have new back pain, leg weakness, numbness, or numbness in the saddle area?
questions.rationale: Back pain with neurologic symptoms can indicate a spinal emergency.

questions.text: Did the pain start suddenly and become severe right away?
questions.rationale: Sudden severe pain can indicate a more urgent urinary or abdominal problem.

red_flags.label: Possible urinary retention
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe being unable to pass urine, or a painful full bladder with little or no output?

red_flags.label: Visible blood in urine
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe pink, red, brown, or otherwise visibly bloody urine?

red_flags.label: Fever or chills with urinary symptoms
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report fever, chills, or sweats together with urinary symptoms?

red_flags.label: Flank pain
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report flank pain, side pain, or back pain that suggests kidney involvement?

red_flags.label: Back pain with neurologic symptoms
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe new back pain together with leg weakness, leg numbness, saddle numbness, or new leakage of urine?

red_flags.label: Severe sudden pain
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe pain that started suddenly and is severe, or rapidly worsening?
